summary: Limited datauser to 100MB of storage under /srv/data on node1, enforced by the filesystem (XFS user quota), persisted across a full node reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: Ubuntu 16.04, single ext4 root filesystem, no separate partition for /srv/data
Installed quota tooling, created local user datauser

Created a 300MB loopback image at /srv/data.img; found ext4 quota unusable (kernel 4.4.0-210-generic lacks quota_v2 module) so reformatted as XFS, which has quota support built directly into this kernel (CONFIG_XFS_QUOTA=y)
Added /etc/fstab entry mounting /srv/data.img at /srv/data as XFS with the uquota option for persistence, then mounted it
Set datauser's XFS user quota to bsoft=100m bhard=100m on /srv/data and chowned the directory to datauser
Verified enforcement pre-reboot: wrote 90MB successfully, then a further write failed with 'Disk quota exceeded' exactly at 100MB; cleaned up test files, quota returned to 0/100M
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime, mount/quota state (Accounting: ON, Enforcement: ON)
Issued `shutdown -r now` via a backgrounded sudo command so the exec call acknowledged before the node disconnected
Polled node1 until exec was reachable again (initial poll got ssh connection refused, confirming the node was actually down)
Verified new boot_id and uptime start time post-restart, confirming an actual reboot occurred
Verified /srv/data remounted automatically via fstab with usrquota, quota Accounting/Enforcement ON, and datauser's 100M/100M limit persisted
Re-ran the write test post-reboot: 150MB write attempt failed with 'Disk quota exceeded' after exactly 100MB written, proving the filesystem-enforced limit survived the restart
Cleaned up test file; final state is /srv/data empty, quota at 0/100M for datauser

evidence.requirement: Filesystem-level 100MB quota configured for datauser under /srv/data
evidence.summary: xfs_quota limit set bsoft=100m bhard=100m for datauser on /srv/data (XFS loopback mount with usrquota), confirmed via report showing 100M/100M limits

evidence.requirement: Quota is enforced by the kernel/filesystem itself (not just tracked)
evidence.summary: datauser wrote 90MB successfully; a further 20MB write failed mid-write with kernel error 'Disk quota exceeded' at exactly 100MB used, confirmed by xfs_quota report

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline of boot identity and quota-enforced service/data
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 9094f607-..., uptime start, and confirmed /srv/data mounted with usrquota and Accounting/Enforcement ON before restart

evidence.requirement: Node restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded `shutdown -r now` returned ACK_REBOOT_ISSUED to the exec caller before the node went down

evidence.requirement: Node actually went down and came back (changed boot identity)
evidence.summary: SSH connection refused during reboot, then exec available again; boot_id changed to fe64b2f3-... and uptime start time advanced, proving an actual reboot

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of the quota-enforced mount and data
evidence.summary: After reboot, /srv/data auto-remounted via fstab with usrquota, Accounting/Enforcement ON, datauser's 100M/100M limit intact; write test again failed with Disk quota exceeded at 100MB, then cleaned up leaving quota at 0/100M
